findings.text: non-blocking: plan_blocker_state derives effective_status from str(plan.get("status") or "draft") at reckon/roadmap.py:1264, and its persisted-placeholder guard tests plan.get("status") at :1244, where the roadmap loop had derived both from _status(plan) (reckon/roadmap.py:627, workflow_status preferred over status) and passed that value into effective_status at the placeholder's former site. The roadmap's row now reports a status source its caller used to override, so a caller whose inventory row carries a workflow_status differing from status (reckon/mcp_discovery.py:303 builds such a key) gets a different effective_status and a differently-armed placeholder. It is latent today: every current caller supplies workflow_status equal to status (reckon/serve.py:2071-2073 writes it from status; discovery rows carry no workflow_status at all, so _inventory_row defaults it to status), which is why this is recorded non-blocking rather than as a regression. The assembly should take its workflow status as an argument the way it takes dependency_blockers, so the caller's own status notion is not silently replaced.

non-blocking: mcp_views._blocking remains a third assembly of the same fact — explicit blocked_by rows, unresolved dependencies and split_unpassed_gates (reckon/mcp_views.py:2552-2565) — and it satisfies neither the held-path nor the plan-level-decision population this node added to plan_blocker_state, so the MCP resource summary can still report an open plan the roadmap reports blocked. The owning file is reckon/mcp_views.py and the addition duplicates rather than extends it: plan_blocker_state is a superset of _blocking's computation with a different signature. This is outside the node's declared write paths and the node's goal names the served view only, so it does not hold the node; it is the same defect one surface further out and belongs in a follow-up node.

non-blocking: the fragment states that under the declared negative control — restoring the served view's own assembly — the decision-held plan disagrees at 2 failed / 3 passed / EXIT=1, but no log for that arm is on disk: the logs directory holds only negative-control.log, which is the second, released-argument control (2 failed / 3 passed, EXIT=1), and the manifest names only that one. The claim itself is consistent — baseline_suite records test_the_served_view_and_the_roadmap's parity case and the decision-held case failing at 9608e78d5 in base-suite.log — so the guard is demonstrably aimed, but half the negative-control evidence in the record cannot be reopened by a later reader. A claimed red arm should be a log with a bare EXIT= line, as the second control is.

item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that serve._derive_lifecycle takes each plan's blocker list from the roadmap assembly as section 51 specifies; at 3a8aba681 reckon/serve.py:2081 calls roadmap.plan_blocker_state and the loop keeps no assembly of its own (no split_unpassed_gates, no effective_status call), and the follow-on released-argument gap the previous review recorded at review-records/...at-74db0ba1...json is closed at reckon/serve.py:2035 and :2084.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits 74db0ba14/890ef73d2/3a8aba681, changed_paths inside the declared scope, after_suite at 890ef73d2 with one failure also present in baseline_suite, a negative_control_log whose last line is a bare EXIT=1, and an outside_scope entry for the two base-arm git-dependent failures and the untriaged shell-geometry test.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares reckon/serve.py, reckon/roadmap.py, tests/test_the_served_view_reads_the_roadmaps_blockers.py, the evidence fragment and a figures directory; git diff --stat 9608e78d5 3a8aba681 changes exactly those first four files (423 insertions, 94 deletions) and no figure, and the fragment's element ids are node-prefixed.

justifications.durability: tests/test_the_served_view_reads_the_roadmaps_blockers.py:180 asserts the two surfaces agree plan by plan and base-suite.log shows it red at 9608e78d5 with 'served {} vs roadmap {decision: {transport}}', the released branch is falsified by a real mutation in negative-control.log ('served {'persisted': {'unrecorded'}} vs roadmap {}', 2 failed, EXIT=1), and no assertion compares a value against the fixture input it was handed; the parity comparison does not cover a dependency-blocked plan, and the gate ran at 890ef73d2 rather than at the docs-only head.
justifications.evidence: base-suite.log (9608e78d5, 367 passed/5 failed/1 skipped/EXIT=1) and head-suite.log (890ef73d2, 371 passed/1 failed/1 skipped/EXIT=1) are recorded in the manifest with identical literal commands, the two base-only new-test failures are the guards reddening on the pre-change code, and the remaining base extras are attributed in outside_scope to a .git-less archive export — but the fragment's declared own-assembly control has no log on disk, so one claimed red arm cannot be reopened.
justifications.fit: plan_blocker_state at reckon/roadmap.py:1192 sits beside plan_level_decisions and unsettled_decisions in the module that owns the assembly, follows the surrounding long-docstring and per-kind-row idiom, and the exported rename to plans_released_by_cleared_blockers names the mechanism with no plan, sprint, gate-ID or ticket identifier in any added name or comment.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/serve.py:2081 now sources blocking, effective_status, section_gate_blockers and decision_blockers from roadmap.plan_blocker_state, the released set comes from the same exported read at :2035, and the loop keeps no assembly, so the two surfaces answer one call — short of full marks only because the assembly re-derives its workflow status itself (reckon/roadmap.py:1264) instead of taking the caller's.
justifications.reuse: the addition collapses two of the repository's three blocker assemblies onto one owner (reckon/roadmap.py:1192, reached from :3452 and reckon/serve.py:2081), which is consolidation rather than a fork; it does not reach mcp_views._blocking at reckon/mcp_views.py:2552, a third partial assembly of the same fact that the node's declared scope excluded, so the search found one remaining duplicate and this score reflects that residual.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 9608e78d5 3a8aba681 lists only reckon/serve.py, reckon/roadmap.py, the new test file and the declared evidence fragment, the third commit is documentation only, and no plan or sprint state was touched.
